authority_note: tag 1.4 is a tagged upstream release commit; this manifest is the final machine-readable authority for the P43 side of the role-artifact compatibility matrix.

source.verification: git fetch origin +refs/tags/1.4:refs/tags/p43-authority resolved to this exact SHA; fetched fresh via git archive and extracted into ~/p43-build/source on q3. Re-verified 2026-08-23: `git cat-file -t` confirms the object is a real commit in this repo, `git tag --points-at` confirms tag 1.4 points at it, and it is reachable via origin/1.4-branch.

build.image_digest_read: docker image inspect icecream/farm-node:ubuntu22-gcc11-boost174 --format '{{.RepoDigests}} {{.Id}}' on q3, live -- not hardcoded from any prior report. RepoDigest and Id both equal this value on q3.
build.recipe: autogen.sh && configure && make -j24, all inside the pinned container image above; dependencies resolved entirely from the container's system packages
build.tweaks_applied: none -- autogen.sh emitted only benign AC_TRY_COMPILE/AC_PROG_LIBTOOL obsolescence warnings (expected for this AC_PREREQ([2.63]) configure.ac); make emitted only a benign docbook2x-missing warning for man-page generation; BUILD-EXIT=0

tar.layout: tar -cf p43-root.tar -C p43-root . -- unpacks flat to obj/{scheduler,daemon,client}/... + MANIFEST.tsv at its own root, a drop-in bind-source for farm.py's /work mount

runtime_dependencies: ldd on every linked binary below resolves entirely to /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/* system libraries inside the pinned image; nothing else from the build tree is dlopened, so the files listed here are the complete runtime root

version_probe.note: rejects --version as an unrecognized option but still emits its startup banner on that same invocation
no --version flag exists in this era; identity read from the embedded startup-banner string
shell script with no embedded version marker in either era; sha256 is the sole identity anchor
the host-side TSV record is hash-pinned too, so a tampered TSV (without also re-signing this committed JSON) is caught the same way as a tampered binary
